newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister calls for carmaker bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister calls for carmaker bankruptcy.

text.p: A senior Russian minister called on Tuesday for the bankruptcy authorities to start proceedings against Russia's biggest carmaker, AvtoVAZ, which the government says is one of the country's biggest tax debtors.
First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, who is in charge of economic policy, asked for the Federal Bankruptcy Administration to initiate proceedings against AO AvtoVAZ.
AvtoVAZ, which makes the Lada car, is Russia's eighth biggest company by sales and with a workforce of 114,000, its fifth biggest employer, according to Ekspert magazine.
The government says AvtoVAZ owes 2.8 trillion roubles in taxes. Officials said its total debt to the public sector and suppliers was 11 trillion roubles.

"We are forced to ask (bankruptcy administration chairman) Pyotr Mostovoi to initiate bankruptcy proceedings. And then we will wait for proposals from AvtoVAZ and consider them," Potanin said during a meeting of the government commission on payments.
Potanin's predecessor as first deputy premier in charge of the economy and chairman of the commission was AvtoVAZ chairman Vladimir Kadannikov.
Russia's economy has been crippled by a web of unpaid bills, in which companies owe each other and the government money, and the government owes companies money.
But the International Monetary Fund has withheld payment of the latest instalment of its $10 billion loan to Russia because of concern about poor tax revenues.
As a result the Russian government has got tough, closing tax loopholes and threatening to have the largest tax debtors declared bankrupt. It says tax revenues have picked up in the last few months.
